title: Token Priority Capacity Arbitration Field Manual
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:
This field manual defines a pragmatic, operator-focused procedure for token-priority capacity arbitration across mixed inference workloads (interactive text generation, streaming chat, batch embeddings, and reranking). It codifies SLO targets, error budget-based arbitration rules, telemetry signals, and step-by-step operations for automated and manual interventions.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: provide runbooked steps to (1) detect cross-tenant or cross-workload contention, (2) arbitrate limited GPU pool capacity using token-priority and tenant-weighted policies, and (3) safely escalate canary capacity or throttle non-critical traffic while preserving critical SLOs.
- Scope: applicable to Redwood Dedicated and Hosted inference clusters that run mixed-mode tenants on shared pools (GPU node pools that host streaming/generation and batch embedding jobs). Not intended for isolated single-tenant private deployments unless explicitly enabled.

Definitions and key concepts:
- Token-priority: per-request cost tag representing expected token production (e.g., tokens_out_est). Used to rank requests for batching and throttling.
- SLO groups: Critical (99.9% p99 latency < 120ms for interactive routes), High (99% p95 latency < 500ms), Best-effort (throughput/latency SLAs not guaranteed).
- Error budget: measured weekly per-service and per-SLO-group; value expressed as the percent of allowable SLO misses before escalation.
- Arbitration window: rolling 15-minute decision window used by the arbitration controller.

SLO and error budget policy (concrete numbers):
- Interactive-generation (Critical): availability SLO 99.9% (p99 latency < 120ms). Weekly error budget = 0.1% of requests.
- Streaming-chat (High): availability SLO 99% (p95 latency < 200ms). Weekly error budget = 1% of requests.
- Embeddings (Best-effort): throughput SLO measured as 95th percentile batch completion < 45s for large jobs; no hard availability SLA.
- Routing fallback rule: if Critical error budget consumed > 30% in last 24h, immediately demote Best-effort to background throttling until budget recovery.

Telemetry signals and dashboards (names used in alerts/queries):
- telemetry.request.latency.p99[route] (ms)
- telemetry.request.latency.p95[route] (ms)
- telemetry.request.qps[route] (rps)
- telemetry.pool.utilization[pool_id] (%)
- telemetry.kvcache.hit_rate[model,tenant] (%)
- telemetry.batch.queue_depth[pool_id] (requests)
- telemetry.error_budget.consumption[service,SLO_group] (%)

Automated arbitration controller (high-level behavior):
1) Every 15s, compute per-route projected error_budget_rate = (observed_miss_rate * weight).
2) If any Critical SLO group has >50% of weekly error budget consumed in last 24h:
   - Priority action: reduce Best-effort ingress to 10% of normal qps, enable aggressive batching for embeddings, and divert long tail requests to async worker queues.
3) If pool_utilization > 85% and Critical p99 is trending above threshold:
   - Apply per-tenant token-priority cap: reject/queue any incoming request whose tokens_out_est + tenant_token_usage_in_window > tenant_token_cap.
4) If automated measures cannot restore Critical SLOs within arbitration window, trigger manual on-call escalation.

Runbook: detection and immediate mitigation (ordered steps):
1) Detection (automated): alert SRE-runbook/critical-slo-threshold if telemetry.request.latency.p99[interactive] > 120ms for >3 consecutive minutes AND telemetry.pool.utilization > 80%.
2) Initial mitigation (automated, run automatically once per alert):
   a) Throttle Best-effort routes to 20% of baseline using traffic-shaper policy.
   b) Turn on KV-cache aggressive mode (cache-ttl=60s) for repeated prefixes.
   c) Increase batch size tolerance for embeddings from 64 to 256 where memory allows (see safe-limits table).
3) If within next 10 minutes p99 remains > 120ms:
   a) Enact token-priority admission (see token cap calculation below).
   b) Notify on-call (pager) and create incident with priority P1.

Token cap calculation (example):
- Tenant_token_cap = max( min_pool_tokens * tenant_share, baseline_avg_tokens * 1.5 )
- Where min_pool_tokens = floor(pool_gpu_mem_mb / 2000) * 1024 (rough heuristic), tenant_share = tenant_committed_weight / total_weights.

Manual on-call escalation and play actions (P1):
1) Verify dashboard signals: p99, p95, qps, pool_utilization, batch_queue_depth.
2) If a single model causes tail latency: add model to live-denylist for new large requests (commands below).
3) If multi-tenant saturation: shift selected non-critical tenants to a spare burst pool (if available) using the routing control-plane CLI.
4) If no spare capacity: coordinate with infra to spin a pre-warmed pool (escalation matrix: infra on-call -> data-center on-call -> exec). Estimated spin-up: 10–18 minutes for Dedicated G4-like nodes.

Commands and snippets (examples):
- Denylist a model from receiving new large sessions:
  curl -X POST https://admin.internal/api/v1/pools/POOL_ID/denylist -d '{"model":"gpt-open-14x","reason":"p99-tail-mitigation"}' 
- Throttle a route to 20%:
  rctl apply --pool POOL_ID --route embed.bulk --rate 0.2

Safe-limits table (reference for automated batch changes):
| GPU mem (GB) | max_batch_emb | max_stream_batch | notes |
| 8            | 64            | 8                | small models only |
| 24           | 256           | 32               | moderate models |
| 80           | 1024          | 128              | requires quantized kernels |

Canary capacity escalation procedure (when to use and how):
- Use when arbitration controller repeatedly demotes Best-effort and p99 remains high for Critical routes for >30 minutes.
Steps:
1) Select 1–2 pre-warmed nodes from pool-tagged canary.
2) Route 15% of interactive traffic to canary nodes using canary route policy with traffic weight ramp: 5% -> 10% -> 15% over 6 minutes.
3) Monitor p99 and cpu/gpu utilization on canary. If p99 improves by >20% relative to baseline and no errors, promote additional nodes in 10-minute increments.
4) If canary fails (p95 or p99 worse by >10%), rollback routing immediately and mark canary nodes for forensic review.

Capacity planning guidance (quarterly):
- Inputs: 95th qps growth forecast, new model onboarding schedule, holiday/marketing events calendar, observed p99 headroom per pool.
- Reserve rule: maintain 15% spare GPU headroom for Critical SLOs and additional 10% buffer for predictable promotional spikes.
- Tenant onboarding gating: require load profile (qps, tokens/session, typical prompt length) and an SLO target before allowing mixed tenancy on a shared pool.

Incident review and follow-up actions (minimal template):
- Title: short description
- Impacted services and SLO groups
- Timeline of key events (detection -> mitigations -> resolution)
- Root cause hypothesis and verification steps
- Decision log for arbitration actions taken (who approved tenant demotions / canary spin-up)
- Remediation items (owners and due dates)
- Post-incident capacity adjustments and budget policy changes

Ownership and roles:
- SRE on-call: initial mitigation and paging.
- Runtime Platform team: enact model-level denylist and routing changes.
- Infra provisioning: spin extra nodes and validate network overlays.
- Product/security: approve any cross-tenant QoS changes for regulated customers.

Telemetry and alert tuning notes (common gotchas):
- Avoid alerting on rolling-average p99 without concurrent utilization signal — otherwise noisy.
- Use mutually corroborating signals (p99 up AND queue_depth rising AND pool_utilization > 70%).
- Track error budget burn rate per tenant to enable proactive conversations with product/CS.

Appendix A — example arbitration YAML policy:
---
name: "token-priority-arbitrator"
window: 900  # 15 minutes in seconds
rules:
  - name: "critical-preserve"
    when: "error_budget.consumption[interactive] > 0.3 and pool.utilization > 0.75"
    actions:
      - throttle_routes: ["embed.bulk", "embed.async"]
      - set_mode: {kv_cache: 'aggressive'}
  - name: "stalling-queue"
    when: "batch.queue_depth > 50 and p99[interactive] > 0.9*threshold"
    actions:
      - token_cap: {type: 'tenant_weighted', window: 900}
      - notify: ['oncall']

Appendix B — post-incident checklist for capacity improvements:
1) Re-run predictive capacity simulation with incident traffic profile.
2) Adjust reservation targets for pools impacted; consider dedicated lane for top-10 tenants by qps.
3) Add synthetic canary tests simulating long-prompt sessions to the canary-runner harness.
4) Incrementally raise embedding batch safe-limits where kernel telemetry proves stable.

Document maintenance:
- Owner: Platform SRE (engineering).
- Review cadence: quarterly and after any P1 where arbitration actions were taken.
- Change log: maintain brief notes on the Confluence page comments for each update.

Contact and escalation matrix:
- Primary SRE on-call: page via PagerDuty (team: platform-sre)
- Infra on-call: infra-pager (channel: #infra-oncall)
- Runtime Platform lead: linnea.berg@redwood.ai
- Product escalation: product-ops@redwood.ai

End of field manual.
